summary: This code defines a function called sayHello that takes an optional person's first name and returns a greeting. If no name is provided, it defaults to greeting 'World', otherwise it greets the person by their name. The function is then called without arguments, which will output 'Hello World!'

explanations.3: The function parameter has a default value of an empty string, so you can call sayHello() without passing any arguments. The type hint 'string' means this parameter must be a string, and the return type ': string' means the function always returns a string.
explanations.5: This uses a ternary operator (the ? and :) which is a shorthand if-else. It checks if firstname is empty; if yes, use 'World!', otherwise use the firstname value passed in.
